description:
Mirror the file transaction kernel's prepared-rollback failure points in the in-memory conformance backend so the shared crash matrix can exercise identical observable edges.

## Background

The JSON backend invokes `RepositoryBeforeReverseAction`, `RepositoryAfterReverseAction`, and `RepositoryBeforeRollbackDecision` while recovering a prepared transaction. The in-memory backend currently restores the original state atomically without invoking those configured failure points, so the epic's cross-backend rollback crash coverage cannot observe or retry the same edges. This is a conformance-seam gap: the durable journal protocol and semantic old/new recovery outcomes remain unchanged.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: In-memory prepared recovery invokes `RepositoryBeforeReverseAction` and `RepositoryAfterReverseAction` in reverse live-action order and invokes `RepositoryBeforeRollbackDecision` before the semantic restore completes.
- [hard] REQ-02: An injected rollback-edge failure retains prepared recovery residue so a later clean session retries and converges to the original state.
- [hard] REQ-03: Existing-root actions participate in the rollback sequence while staged absent-data-root actions are excluded consistently with the file transaction kernel.
- [hard] REQ-04: Focused tests prove the injection order, retry behavior, and unchanged committed-recovery and successful prepared-recovery outcomes without changing journal or transaction semantics.
title: Mirror prepared rollback failure points in memory recovery
